밤 11시, 배치의 DML이 모두 같은 대기에서 멈췄다: 11 p.m.: every DML in the batch stops on the same wait
대량 적재 배치가 돌던 밤 11시, 모니터링에 세션 여러 개가 같은 대기: At 11 p.m., during a bulk-load batch, monitoring shows many sessions on the same wait event: log file switch (checkpoint incomplete). They stall for a few seconds, resume, stall again, and the batch falls far behind schedule.
이름에 답이 들어 있습니다. 로그를 전환(switch)하려는데 체크포인트: The name holds the answer: a log switch is wanted, but a checkpoint has not completed. What do redo logs have to do with checkpoints, that writing redo would wait for writing data files?
Database Reference는 이 대기를 \"세션이 다음 로그로 넘: The Database Reference describes this wait as waiting for a log switch because the session cannot wrap into the next log. Why it cannot is the topic of this lesson.
커밋은 리두만 쓴다. 데이터 블록은 버퍼 캐시에 남는다: A commit writes only redo. Data blocks stay in the buffer cache
\"COMMIT의 여정\"에서 본 대로, 커밋할 때 디스크에 반드시 써야: As "The journey of a COMMIT" showed, the only thing that must be on disk at commit time is redo. Once LGWR writes the redo to the online redo log, the commit is done. The changed data blocks stay in the buffer cache; a buffer whose contents differ from the data file is a dirty buffer.
더티 버퍼를 데이터 파일에 쓰는 것은 DBWn의 일입니다. Concept: Writing dirty buffers to the data files is DBWn's job. According to Concepts, DBWn writes asynchronously when possible, and writes when it cannot find clean reusable buffers or when the checkpoint needs to advance. Since it does not write at every commit, a block changed many times needs to be written only once.
그래서 정전이 나도 커밋한 데이터는 안전합니다. 데이터 파일에 아직 없는: That is why committed data is safe even in a power cut: changes not yet in the data files are in the redo. But that redo must stay as needed redo until those blocks are written to the data files.
+ 더티 버퍼 4개 (데이터 파일엔 아직 없음): + 4 dirty buffers (not yet in data files)
체크포인트 위치: 복구를 어디서부터 시작할지: The checkpoint position: where recovery must start
Concepts는 <span class=\"term\">체크포인트</sp: Concepts defines a checkpoint as a data structure that indicates the checkpoint position. The position is determined by the oldest dirty buffer in the buffer cache; if the instance crashes, redo only needs to be applied from this point, because earlier changes are already in the data files.
체크포인트 위치는 컨트롤 파일과 각 데이터 파일 헤더에 저장됩니다. 문서: The checkpoint position is stored in the control file and in each data file header. The documentation lists the purposes of checkpoints: reduce recovery time after an instance or media failure, ensure dirty buffers are written to disk regularly, and ensure all committed data is written to disk during a consistent shutdown.
체크포인트 위치보다 뒤의 리두가 바로 \"인스턴스 복구에 필요한 리두\": Redo after the checkpoint position is exactly the redo needed for instance recovery. An online redo log group holding that redo cannot be overwritten yet. The incident in scene 6 comes from this.
Concepts에 따르면 <span class=\"term\">CKPT<: According to Concepts, CKPT updates the control file and data file headers with checkpoint information and signals DBWn to write blocks to disk. CKPT itself does not write data blocks to data files; DBWn does the actual writing.
평소에는 <span class=\"term\">증분 체크포인트</span: Normally incremental checkpoints run. According to the documentation, DBWn checks at least every three seconds whether it has work, writes the oldest dirty buffers first, and moves the checkpoint position forward. For these, CKPT records the position in the control file only, not in the data file headers.
리눅스에서 <code>ps -ef | grep ora_</code>로 보: On Linux, ps -ef | grep ora_ shows processes such as ora_ckpt_ORCL and ora_dbw0_ORCL. The lesson "SGA, PGA and background processes" revisits them with the other mandatory processes.
- 오래된 더티 버퍼 2개 씀 → 위치 SCN 5,600: - 2 oldest dirty buffers written → position SCN 5,600
로그 스위치가 나면 체크포인트가 시작된다: A log switch starts a checkpoint
그룹 1이 차서 LGWR가 그룹 2로 넘어갑니다. Concepts는 온라: Group 1 fills and LGWR moves on to group 2. Concepts lists an online redo log switch as one of the events that start a thread checkpoint. The checkpoint completes only when DBWn has written to the data files all dirty buffers protected by group 1's redo.
그 전까지 그룹 1은 인스턴스 복구에 아직 필요합니다. <code>V$L: Until then group 1 is still needed for instance recovery. In V$LOG such a group shows STATUS ACTIVE; once its checkpoint is complete and it is no longer needed for recovery, it shows INACTIVE. In ARCHIVELOG mode, ARCn must also have copied it before it can be reused.
그룹이 다시 쓰이려면 두 가지가 끝나야 합니다. 체크포인트(데이터 블록이: Before a group can be reused, two things must be finished: its checkpoint (data blocks written to data files) and, in ARCHIVELOG mode, its archiving (redo copied). Scene 9 of "Archivelog and RMAN" is the second one getting stuck; scene 6 here is the first.
사례: 한 바퀴 돌아왔는데 체크포인트가 안 끝났다: Case: a full lap later, the checkpoint is not finished
배치는 리두를 아주 빨리 만듭니다. 200MB짜리 그룹 세 개가 1분도: The batch generates redo very fast. Three 200 MB groups fill in under a minute, and after group 3 LGWR wants to wrap back to group 1. But DBWn has not finished writing the dirty buffers that group 1 protects. Group 1 is still ACTIVE.
Database Reference의 설명 그대로, 그 로그의 체크포인트가: Exactly as the Database Reference says, wrapping cannot be performed because the checkpoint for that log has not completed. With nowhere to write redo, every DML session that needs to generate redo waits on log file switch (checkpoint incomplete). The moment the checkpoint completes they resume, and on the next lap they stall again.
사례: 대기 시간과 로그 전환 횟수를 본다: Case: look at wait time and log switch frequency
먼저 이 대기가 얼마나 쌓였는지 <code>V$SYSTEM_EVENT</: First, check how much of this wait has accumulated with V$SYSTEM_EVENT. Then count log switches per hour from V$LOG_HISTORY. Dozens of switches an hour during the batch mean the logs are small for the rate at which redo is generated.
AWR 보고서가 있다면 같은 시간대의 상위 대기 이벤트와 초당 리두 크기: If you have an AWR report, also look at the top wait events and redo size per second for the same period. The AWR lesson in DBA labs stage 7 walks through this.
Performance Tuning Guide는 이 대기에 대해 \"리두: For this wait, the Performance Tuning Guide says to check whether there are too few or too small redo logs. DBWn's write speed (the disks) may also be a suspect, but look at the log layout first.
~ 23시대 로그 전환 74회: ~ 74 log switches in the 11 p.m. hour
사례: 로그를 키우거나 늘려 체크포인트에 시간을 준다: Case: make the logs bigger or more numerous to give checkpoints time
문서의 대책은 리두 로그의 크기나 개수를 늘리는 것입니다. 한 바퀴 도는: The documented fix is to increase the size or number of redo logs. If one lap takes longer, DBWn has time to finish the checkpoint in between. While the database runs, add bigger groups with ALTER DATABASE ADD LOGFILE, and drop the small groups once they become INACTIVE.
크기를 정할 때는 <code>V$INSTANCE_RECOVERY</cod: When choosing a size, OPTIMAL_LOGFILE_SIZE (MB) in V$INSTANCE_RECOVERY helps. The Database Reference describes it as the size to configure all online redo logs to be at least. The value is computed when FAST_START_MTTR_TARGET, from the next scene, is set.
CURRENT나 ACTIVE인 그룹은 지울 수 없습니다. <code>AL: A CURRENT or ACTIVE group cannot be dropped. Make it INACTIVE with ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE and ALTER SYSTEM CHECKPOINT first, then drop it, and delete the Linux file separately.
FAST_START_MTTR_TARGET: 복구 시간으로 체크포인트를 조: FAST_START_MTTR_TARGET: tune checkpoints by recovery time
체크포인트를 자주 밀면 인스턴스 복구가 빨라지지만 DBWn의 쓰기가 늘고: Pushing the checkpoint often makes instance recovery faster but increases DBWn's writes; pushing it rarely does the opposite. According to the Performance Tuning Guide, FAST_START_MTTR_TARGET is the time in seconds it should take to start the instance and perform cache recovery, with a maximum of 3600 seconds (one hour).
오라클은 이 목표에 맞춰 증분 체크포인트의 속도를 스스로 정합니다. <c: Oracle sets the pace of incremental checkpoints to meet this target. Compare the target with the current estimate using TARGET_MTTR and ESTIMATED_MTTR in V$INSTANCE_RECOVERY. The documentation says that when using it, older settings such as LOG_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL and LOG_CHECKPOINT_TIMEOUT should be disabled.
\"인스턴스와 데이터베이스\" 7장면의 인스턴스 복구가 바로 이 시간입니: Instance recovery in scene 7 of "Instance and database" is exactly this time: SMON applies redo from the checkpoint position (roll forward) and undoes uncommitted changes (roll back).
정리: 커밋은 리두로, 데이터 파일은 체크포인트로: Recap: commits go through redo; data files catch up through checkpoints
커밋할 때는 리두만 쓰고, 고친 블록은 더티 버퍼로 남습니다. DBWn이: A commit writes only redo; changed blocks remain as dirty buffers. As DBWn writes those buffers to the data files, the checkpoint position moves forward, and CKPT records it in the control file and data file headers.
체크포인트 위치보다 뒤의 리두가 든 그룹은 덮어쓸 수 없습니다. 리두가: A group holding redo after the checkpoint position cannot be overwritten. If redo laps the logs faster than checkpoints complete, DML stalls on log file switch (checkpoint incomplete). The fix is the size and number of logs, and the recovery-time goal is set with FAST_START_MTTR_TARGET.
리두 로그는 \"변경의 기록\"이면서 \"아직 데이터 파일에 없는 변경의: The redo log is both a record of changes and insurance for changes not yet in the data files. Only when the insurance ends (the checkpoint) can its space be reused.
~ 리두 → 더티 버퍼 → DBWn 쓰기 → 체크포인트 위치: ~ redo → dirty buffers → DBWn writes → checkpoint position
명령 한 줄의 여정: The journey of one command line
리두를 만들지 않는 조회는 대부분 그대로 돌기 때문에, \"DB가 반쯤: Queries that generate no redo mostly keep running, so a report that "the database is half frozen" is typical of this incident. The wait event query in DBA labs stage 7 shows it at once.
